observations.why: The speaker enacts a decisional authority by declaring adoption on behalf of the collective, performing a hierarchical move rather than proposing or negotiating.
The performance frames the choice in proportional cost-benefit terms, justifying the decision by quantified advantage — a proportionality argument.
The speaker commits the organization to a timeline, enacting authority over scheduling — a commissive that binds the collective to a plan.
The note-taker records the decision as settled, ratifying the hierarchical adoption act in summary form.
The summary records the proportionality justification, preserving the cost-benefit framing of the decision.
The summary records the timeline commitment, ratifying the authority-ranking commissive act.
